claims.text: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Replacing 20% of the Hf content with Al produces the nominal composition Hf0.8Al0.2MoTaTiZr.
The Al-modified alloy will retain a single-phase BCC solid solution across the operating temperature range.
Al addition will produce only slight short-range ordering.
The modified alloy will remain homogeneous without detrimental phase separation.
Replacing heavy Hf atoms with lighter Al atoms lowers the alloy's average atomic weight.
The reduction in average atomic weight caused by Hf-to-Al substitution will reduce alloy density.
Al addition will induce lattice distortion that contributes to solid-solution strengthening.
Al addition may foster coherent nanoscale precipitates that enhance high-temperature performance.
The modified alloy's density will be 10–15% lower than that of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will retain a room-temperature yield strength near 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain a yield strength near 850 MPa at 1000 °C.
Mechanical performance will be assessed by uniaxial tensile testing at room temperature and 1000 °C at a strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
Al content may destabilize the alloy at elevated temperature by inducing unwanted ordering or phase separation.
A density reduction below 10% is specified as a falsifying outcome.
Secondary phases associated with a yield-strength decrease exceeding 10% at room temperature or 1000 °C are specified as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator requires a homogeneous single-phase BCC solid solution without phase separation, whereas the mechanism invokes coherent nanoscale precipitates as a possible source of high-temperature strengthening. Distinct precipitates are not straightforwardly compatible with the asserted single-phase state.

The phrase 'approximately 20 at.% Hf with Al' can imply 20 at.% Al in the total alloy, but Hf0.8Al0.2MoTaTiZr normalizes to only 4 at.% Al and 16 at.% Hf. The formula instead represents replacement of 20% of the original Hf sublattice.
